# Temple Scroll Column 60 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 60 where the three translators significantly diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 60:3 — "redeemer of blood" vs. "avenger of blood" vs. "victim's nearest relative"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "redeemer of blood" | Literal go'el ha-dam — preserving the root g-'-l "to redeem" |
| LOGOS | "avenger of blood" | Standard scholarly and translational rendering |
| PNEUMA | "the victim's nearest relative" | Explains the social role without the technical term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "avenger of blood" (LOGOS). This is the universally recognized rendering in English biblical scholarship. EMET's "redeemer" imports redemption theology; PNEUMA's paraphrase loses the technical legal term.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 60:4 — "burn out" vs. "purge" vs. "purge the stain"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "burn out the innocent blood" | Literal bi'arta — from the root b-'-r |
| LOGOS | "purge the guilt of innocent blood" | Standard Deuteronomic purge formula with "guilt" clarification |
| PNEUMA | "purge the stain of innocent blood" | Metaphorical addition emphasizing defilement |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "purge the guilt of innocent blood" (LOGOS). "Guilt" makes the legal concept explicit; PNEUMA's "stain" adds a metaphor not in the Hebrew.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 60:5 — "boundary-marker" vs. "boundary marker" vs. "boundary stone"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "boundary-marker" | Compound for gevul — the territorial boundary |
| LOGOS | "boundary marker" | Same without hyphenation |
| PNEUMA | "boundary stone" | Specifies the physical object — a stone marker |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "boundary marker" (LOGOS). No hyphen needed in English. PNEUMA's "boundary stone" specifies a material not mentioned in the text, though stones were commonly used.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 60:7 — "turning-aside" vs. "wrongdoing" vs. "falsely"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a turning-aside" | Literal sarah — deviation from truth |
| LOGOS | "wrongdoing" | Standard English legal term for the false charge |
| PNEUMA | "testifies falsely" | Restructured as a verb phrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "wrongdoing" (LOGOS). EMET's "turning-aside" is opaque in English; PNEUMA's restructuring changes the syntax unnecessarily.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 60:12 — "soul for soul" vs. "life for life"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "soul for soul" | Literal nefesh — preserving the Hebrew term |
| LOGOS | "life for life" | Standard English rendering of the lex talionis |
| PNEUMA | "life for life" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "life for life" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). In this judicial context, nefesh means "life" not "soul" in the theological sense. The lex talionis formula should use the standard English rendering.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## 60:15 — four-fold fear prohibition

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "let your heart not be faint; do not fear and do not tremble and do not be-terrified" | Literal Hebrew four verbs |
| LOGOS | "do not lose heart; do not be afraid; do not panic; do not be terrified" | Standard English with graduated intensity |
| PNEUMA | "do not be fainthearted; do not be afraid; do not panic or tremble" | Combined last two elements |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. The four distinct prohibitions should be preserved as four distinct English phrases. PNEUMA's combination of the last two loses the rhetorical force. LOGOS's graduated intensity captures the escalating encouragement.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 60:16 — "to save you" vs. "to give you victory"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "to save you" | Literal lehoshi'a — from the root y-sh-' "to save/deliver" |
| LOGOS | "to give you victory" | Military context — the salvation here means battlefield victory |
| PNEUMA | "give you the victory" | Same as LOGOS with article |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "to give you victory" (LOGOS). In the military context of the priest's battle speech, hoshi'a means to grant victory, not spiritual salvation. LOGOS captures this accurately.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
